prize_parts.citation: For the development of ionizable lipid nanoparticles, in which pH-dependent lipid charge and self-assembly allow nucleic acids to be encapsulated, protected in circulation and released inside cells

statement.case_for: I keep B062, and I can answer the chair's question about what the citation honours: the formation principle, meaning encapsulation of nucleic acid in lipid particles built from lipids whose charge depends on pH, with lipid polymorphism governing endosomal release. That is a molecular design rule from physical chemistry, written in terms a non-specialist can follow (a lipid that is neutral in blood and charged in the acidic endosome), and it is a separate achievement from the 2023 Medicine prize, which concerned nucleoside modification of the mRNA cargo and not the carrier. It is the only shortlisted candidate whose effect on what clinicians can do is already large and independently validated, with an approved siRNA drug and mRNA vaccines delivered at very large scale. There is no maturity risk of the kind that attaches to degraders, and the carrier is also what allows later in vivo delivery of base editors and other nucleic-acid tools.
statement.case_against: Attribution is still the weakest part. Six names (Cullis, Madden, Hope, MacLachlan, Anderson, Langer) compete for three places, and my trio places the early encapsulation and ionizable-lipid work above later lipid-library screening and clinical siRNA translation, so it will look incomplete to anyone who weights the later work. Several colleagues also regard parts of this as formulation and not chemistry, and my account of who did what is from memory and not checked against the expert reports. B062 has only two explicit supporters, and the chair's summary shows that B027 is much closer to a majority than my choice. I accept that gap and have not changed my scientific ranking to close it.

responses.point: Brzezinski moved to B027 with Crews, Deshaies and Handa, saying the three names map onto the PROTAC and glue branches and that B062 is a harder fit because six people compete for three places.
responses.response: The attribution criticism is fair and I do not claim B062 is tidy. But the same three-name test is not passed cleanly by B027 either: Crews and Deshaies (2001) and Handa (2010) are two discoveries made by different groups nearly a decade apart, and Ciulli, Sakamoto and Ito are left out. My difficulty is that B027 has no approved drug, so what clinicians can do with it is still prospective. I do not dismiss it, since the induced-proximity mechanism is clear and well reproduced, and I keep it as my first alternative. I will not rank it first only because it has more supporters.

responses.point: Sparr, who also ranks B062 first, now names Cullis, Madden and Hope and says her trio favours early Vancouver encapsulation work over the later library and siRNA-clinical work of Anderson, Langer and MacLachlan.
responses.response: We now give the same trio, and I think that is the defensible reading: the citation honours the principle of forming and releasing the particle, not the later optimisation. I accept her view that this leaves out Anderson, MacLachlan and Langer, who made the library screening and siRNA clinical work that moved potency forward, and the citation wording should make clear that it is about the underlying design rule. Where I would add to her chemistry argument is the language of the citation, which should name pH-dependent charge and encapsulation explicitly so that it reads as chemistry and not as a vaccine prize.

responses.point: Linke, as chair, argues B027 is a clear mechanistic principle that can be explained to a broad audience and is reaching late-stage trials, and he moved his third name from Ciulli to Handa.
responses.response: I find the mechanism clear and I agree it can be explained simply, but the same can be said of the LNP design principle. On maturity our views differ: late-stage trials are not patients treated at scale, and Linke himself says the clinical proof is still maturing. I also agree that merging PROTACs and cereblon glues into one citation risks combining two discoveries. Even so, I would call a three-person B027 prize defensible, and if the committee converges there I would not block it. I would put the maturity question to the members who prefer B027 as a condition and not as a footnote.

responses.point: Chabes pairs base editing by Liu alone (B038) with a two-person degradation part (Crews and Handa), and asks whether the committee prefers one coherent achievement or two parts.
responses.response: I prefer one coherent achievement, since a two-part prize built from unrelated fields looks driven by the three-person cap and not by scientific logic, which Chabes himself says. I also keep my view that base editing is early compared with delivery technology, and his own point that the 2020 CRISPR prize makes the framing harder supports that. His Crews and Handa version for B027 is worth noting because it shows the glue and PROTAC branches can be cut either way, which weakens the argument that Deshaies is indispensable.

uncertainties: My account of who contributed what in the lipid nanoparticle history (Cullis, Madden and Hope on early encapsulation and ionizable lipids; Anderson, MacLachlan and Langer on later optimisation and siRNA delivery) is from memory and is unverified.
Whether colleagues who see lipid nanoparticles as formulation will accept a citation worded around pH-dependent charge and self-assembly as chemistry.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader is a reason to defer B027 or only a reason for a careful citation; clinical status of both modalities is from memory.
Whether the committee can reach five votes for any configuration, and whether I should accept B027 as a second-best outcome if B062 does not reach majority.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict or recusal need is apparent from my profile for B062, B027 or B050. My general overlap in peptide and self-assembly research with Emma Sparr, and my work on bioresponsive nanomaterials and biosensing, is scientific closeness and not a personal tie to any credited person. I have no connection to Cullis, Madden, Hope, Anderson, MacLachlan or Langer.
